Circuit: a multi-stage discrete transistor network, 23 components. Five one-port supply symbols (drawn as labelled arrows) set the rails: +15V (#0) on the left vertical rail x~140, +10V (#2) on the bottom rail at x~263, +5V (#6) on the top rail at x~478, +6V (#7) at (489,597), +3V (#13) at (646,903). A GND symbol (#22, drawn rotated at (979,217)) sits at the top right and grounds the long right-hand vertical rail x~940 that runs from y~213 down to y~910.

SITE DECISIONS - all 15 CRITICAL sites explicitly recorded:
  S1 (477,196) deg4 -> JUNCTION. Unmistakable solder dot where the +5V lead-in and the 15-ohm column meet the top rail. A crossing here would strand the +5V symbol and cut R8 off from the rail.
  S2 (643,200) deg3 -> JUNCTION. Solder dot on a tee; the lead drops from the top rail to BJT14's emitter.
  S5 (481,318) deg4 -> CROSSING (agreeing with the tracer default). The horizontal wire between diode #5 and diode #10 makes a clear SEMICIRCULAR HOP over the 15-ohm column at x~481 (hop score 24.4, visible at 5x). This is the drafter's explicit not-connected marker. The other reading would merge n6 into the +5V rail n4, which would short both diodes' junction to +5V and put R8's top, both diode terminals and the whole top rail on one node - clearly not what is drawn.
  S6 (694,341) deg3 -> JUNCTION. Solder dot on a tee where BJT14's base lead drops onto the diode10 -> BJT21 wire.
  S7 (940,346), S13 (938,456), S24 (940,572), S29 (940,710), S37 (940,824) -> all JUNCTION. Five plain tees where a horizontal lead lands on the grounded right rail (BJT21 emitter, the 50k output wire, BJT18 emitter, BJT19 emitter, BJT15 collector respectively). The rail is continuous through each and the lead simply ends on it; reading any of them as a crossing would leave that terminal dangling with no return path to ground.
  S10 (857,429) + S11 (859,435) -> EXPLICIT EDGE GROUPS, i.e. a CROSSING. This is the most important override on the sheet. At 10x the drawing shows an unambiguous semicircular HOP: the horizontal wire coming from R16's right lead (edge e33 -> e28) arcs UP over the vertical wire and continues east as e31 to the ground rail. The tracer split the single drawn hop into two tee sites 6 px apart, so neither 'crossing' nor 'junction' can express it; I used explicit groups instead: site 10 = [[25,29,34],[28,31]], site 11 = 'none'. Group [25,29,34] is the continuous VERTICAL wire (BJT21's base lead from (858,389) down through the two site nodes to (857,503) and on to S25); group [28,31] is the two halves of the ARC, i.e. the horizontal 50k wire passing over it. Consequence of the default (junction): BJT21's base would have been tied to its own emitter and to ground, and BJT11's collector and BJT18's collector would also have been grounded - four transistor terminals wrongly shorted to net 0, and the transistor stage would be dead. With the crossing, n9 becomes a proper 3-terminal signal net (BJT21 base / BJT11 collector / BJT18 collector) and R16's right end still reaches ground through S13, exactly as drawn.
  S17 (132,495) deg3 -> JUNCTION. Solder dot where the +15V arrow's lead meets the left vertical rail.
  S25 (758,578) deg3 -> JUNCTION. Tee with a blob where the descending n9 wire meets BJT18's collector lead and BJT11's collector lead. Not connecting here would leave BJT11's collector lead ending in mid-air.
  S26 (489,597) deg5 -> JUNCTION. The +6V node, drawn with a dot: R8's bottom, R9's top, the +6V arrow and BJT11's emitter lead all terminate here.
  S43 (646,903) deg3 -> JUNCTION. The +3V node: the arrow lead, BJT15's base lead from above and the wire east to R20 meet.
  Non-critical sites left at the tracer default (none are wire-to-wire; all are label ink or already-inside-one-net corners): S4 (the GND stem meeting the right rail - a genuine tee, netlist-neutral), S8/S9 ('15ohm'), S14/S18/S20/S21 ('50kohm'), S16 ('+15V' glyph), S27/S28 ('150ohm'), S30/S33/S34 (three sub-nodes of the same bottom-rail junction at x~493 where R9's bottom lead lands - all one net either way), S31 (bottom-left corner), S32 ('+10V' lead-in dot), S35 ('+10V' glyph), S36/S38/S41 ('50kohm' text touching the wire).

PIN-ORDER FIXES (this is where most of the errors were - five of the nine transistors had collector and emitter transposed). Every transistor on this sheet is drawn rotated 90 degrees: the base bar is HORIZONTAL, the base lead leaves it perpendicular on one side, and collector and emitter leave the bar ends at 45 degrees on the other side. I read each arrowhead at 10x-22x.
  #3 BJT-NPN (360,210): base = the down lead p2 (correct already). The ARROW is on the RIGHT lead, apex at (373,197) with both barbs pointing back down, i.e. pointing AWAY from the bar -> NPN emitter. So emitter = p1 (right, to the +5V rail) and collector = p0 (left, to the +15V rail). Was t0=p1/t2=p0; fixed to t0=p0, t1=p2, t2=p1. Physical check: collector +15V, emitter +5V - correct NPN biasing.
  #15 BJT-PNP (643,834): base = the down lead p1 (correct). The arrowhead (the drafter's two-stroke 'V + tick' glyph) sits on the LEFT lead at (628,839) pointing down-right, i.e. TOWARD the bar -> PNP emitter. So emitter = p2 (left) and collector = p0 (right, to the ground rail). Was t0=p2/t2=p0; fixed to t0=p0, t1=p1, t2=p2.
  #17 BJT-NPN (845,225): all three were wrong. The perpendicular lead is the one going DOWN from the bar at x~843 and then west - that is the BASE (p2, to BJT14's collector). The arrow is at the top of the RIGHT lead, apex (855,212), barbs pointing back down = away from the bar -> emitter = p1 (right, to the ground rail). Collector = p0 (left, to the +5V top rail). Was t0=p1, t1=p0, t2=p2; fixed to t0=p0, t1=p2, t2=p1. Physical check: collector +5V, emitter grounded - textbook.
  #18 BJT-NPN (813,580): base = down lead p2 (correct). Arrow at the top of the RIGHT lead, apex (823,571), pointing away from the bar -> emitter = p0 (right, to the ground rail); collector = p1 (left, onto n9). Was t0=p0/t2=p1; fixed to t0=p1, t1=p2, t2=p0.
  #19 BJT-NPN (826,690): base = the UP lead p2 (correct). Verified at 20x that the dark blob at the left lead's lower end (793,707) is just the thick corner where the diagonal meets the horizontal wire, NOT an arrowhead, while the RIGHT lead carries a clean two-barb arrowhead at (857,690) pointing down-right = away from the bar -> emitter = p0 (right, to the ground rail); collector = p1 (left, onto n11). Was t0=p0/t2=p1; fixed to t0=p1, t1=p2, t2=p0.
  Verified CORRECT and left alone: #11 BJT-PNP (arrow on the lower-left lead pointing up-right into the bar = emitter, t2=p1 already), #12 BJT-PNP (arrow on the upper-left lead pointing down-right into the bar = emitter, t2=p0 already), #14 BJT-PNP (arrow on the upper-left lead pointing into the bar = emitter, t2=p0 already), #21 BJT-NPN (arrow at the top of the right lead pointing away from the bar = emitter, t2=p1 already). All two-terminal parts' ports were checked in the _comps montages and are on real leads; the 'unused port candidate' warnings on #1, #4, #6, #8, #9 and #16 are all value-label ink ('15kohm', '+10V', '+5V', '15ohm', '150ohm', '50kohm') touching the boxes.

CLASSES: I accept all 23 as annotated. One caveat worth recording: diodes #5 (405,330) and #10 (547,335) are drawn with a near-vertical cathode bar that carries a small angled tick at its top end, which at first glance reads like a zener's bent bar. Both are drawn in exactly the same style and both are annotated 'Diode', and there is no second style on the sheet to contrast against, so I did not reclassify - but if the sheet were re-audited these two are the only symbols where 'Zener Diode' would be arguable. The five arrow-with-label symbols are correctly 'V-DC (one port)' supply taps, and #22 is a GND drawn rotated 90 degrees.

UNRESOLVED: nothing electrically ambiguous remains. The only genuinely judgement-based call was the S10/S11 hop, and there the ink (a full semicircular arc) is decisive rather than borderline; the drafter also used the same arc device at S5, so the convention is established on this sheet.
